annotations.title: Assess AI initiative from plain English

description: The front door for one AI investment decision. CALL THIS FIRST when the user describes an AI idea in ordinary language or asks whether it should proceed. It works as a short guided conversation and returns one thing to ask at a time. Pass the proposal unchanged on every call, plus everything the user has answered so far. needs_input: a piece of context (industry, business function, AI type or headcount) could not be read; ask question and pass the answer in its named field. needs_confirmation: show the understood statement, ask the user whether it is right, then call again with confirmed true or with the corrected item. not_enough_to_judge: ask question, the next of at most five plain questions, showing every choice label; pass the id of the choice the user picks in answers. When question is absent, tell the user what is listed in to_find_out and stop. verdict: Accelerate, Fix or Stop, from the user's answers read against the proposal. Where the words of the proposal contradict a favourable answer, the verdict is held at Fix and contradictions quotes those words; show them beside the answer and ask the user which is true. Give the user summary first, then each item in holding_back with what they said and what it needs to become, then first_step; these are written in everyday words, so do not replace them with framework terms. Lead with warning whenever it is present. This tool fills in no score and returns no euro figure, so never state a euro benefit from this result. With a person present, never set confirmed and never pick an answer for them; when they are unsure, pass unknown. WORKING ALONE under your owner's mandate, with nobody to ask, use evidence mode: set answered_by to evidence, pass for each question the answer your evidence supports, and put the exact quote and its source in evidence, as a list of up to three when the answer rests on more than one document. An answer with no quote is counted as not known, so pass unknown when you found nothing; where_to_look says where each answer is usually written down. Answer all five questions in one call: open_questions lists every question still open with its choices, including how the work changes, which the sequence for a person asks only when the other four clear. In evidence mode you check the understood statement against what you read and set confirmed yourself. The verdict then carries provenance: say its statement with the verdict. Where two records disagree on an answer, pass the words of the other record in evidence_against: the answer is counted as not known and conflicts returns both, with the question to put to the owner. Pass industry and employees only as the records state them, with the quote in context_evidence, or unknown: an unquoted company fact counts as not stated and context_defaults says which default was used. Where an approval is still to come before go-live, pass it in pending_approvals with its quote: an Accelerate then goes ahead only once it is given. At a return visit, pass review with previous_brief, the brief_url of the earlier verdict: since_last then says which answers changed and which change moved the verdict. For the person who holds the budget, pass funding with what is asked for the next stage, the alternative and up to three results agreed to release more money: funding comes back beside the verdict with what is still not known, and at a return visit with each agreed result marked met or not met. It never changes the verdict and never says whether to fund. Give the user brief_url, the link to the one-page brief. Organisations under 250 people get questions worded for a smaller firm, with the same rules for every size. Use score_initiative when canonical fields and 0 to 100 scores are already known and a planning range is wanted, score_portfolio for several initiatives, and diagnose_process for measured waste in a running process. Deterministic calculation with no authentication. Anonymous usage telemetry may be sent; set AIBVF_TELEMETRY_DISABLE=1 to opt out.

examples.proposal: We are a 400-person online retailer. We want an AI agent to answer first-line customer queries and issue refunds up to 50 euros on its own.

ai_tier.description: Answer or correction: automation/RPA, GenAI/copilot, or agentic/autonomous. Overrides anything read from proposal.

answered_by.description: Who chose the answers. Omit it when a person answered. Pass evidence only when you work alone under your owner's mandate and answer from evidence you can quote. In evidence mode every answer of a to d needs its entry in evidence, numeric scores are refused, and the verdict says that an agent answered and no person confirmed it.

answers.description: The answers to the guided questions, by question id. Each value is the id of a choice: a, b, c, d, or unknown. Pass every answer given so far on each call. With a person present, pass what the person picked and never pick for them. In evidence mode, pass only the answer your quote supports, and unknown when you found nothing. Answer all five in one call: open_questions returns every question still open with its choices.

assessment_id.description: Optional opaque ID returned by the previous call. Copy it unchanged while continuing the same assessment; omit it for a new idea. Never derive it from proposal text or a person.

brief_includes_proposal.description: Set true only when the owner says the wording of the proposal may travel in brief_url. Without it the link carries the context, the answers and, in evidence mode, the quotes.

confirmed.description: Set true only after the user has seen the understood statement and said it is right. Never set it on behalf of a user who is present. Working alone in evidence mode, set it yourself after checking the reading against what you read.

context_evidence.description: Evidence mode: the quote that states the industry, and the quote that states the number of people. Without one, the value counts as not stated and context_defaults says so. A number of people counts only when the quote shows that number. Never fill in a company fact you cannot quote.

context_stated_by.description: Evidence mode: pass owner only when your owner told you the industry and the number of people. They then need no quote.

employees.description: Number of people in the organisation, or unknown when nobody has stated it. Never estimate it. Under 250 the questions are worded for a smaller firm; unknown keeps the wording for a larger organisation and context_defaults says so. The rules are the same for every size.

evidence.description: Evidence mode: for each answered question, the words the answer rests on and where they were found. An answer of a to d with no quote and source is counted as not known and listed in evidence_missing. Quote the source exactly. Never write a quote yourself. Where an answer rests on more than one document, pass a list of up to three quotes, each with its own source, and never join words from different places into one quote.

evidence_against.description: Evidence mode: where another record says otherwise than your answer, the words of that record and where they were found, by question id. Pass the answer one record supports in answers, its quote in evidence, and the words of the other record here. The answer is then counted as not known and both sets of quotes come back in conflicts, because no rule here picks which record applies today. A later record that reports a change replaces the earlier one, and that is no disagreement. Never leave a record out because it disagrees.

function.description: Answer or correction in canonical or everyday language, for example customer service, procurement, finance or risk. Overrides anything read from proposal.

funding.description: OPTIONAL. The funding record, for the person who holds the budget: what is asked for the next stage, the alternative, and up to three results agreed to release more money. It sits beside the verdict and never changes it. Pass only figures the organisation has stated, never one you worked out. In evidence mode each figure needs its quote and source, or it is not kept. At a return visit pass review.previous_brief and put what was measured in results: the agreed results come back from the earlier link. This tool never says whether to fund.

alternative.description: The cheapest credible other route, including fixing the process as it is.

amount.description: The amount asked, as the organisation states it, in its own currency. Write out 110k as 110000 and 1.2 million as 1200000. Never convert a currency.

amount_eur.description: Older form for an amount in euros. Prefer amount with currency EUR.

currency.description: The currency the quote states. Leave it out when the quote states none.

quote.description: The words as written in the source, at least a few words long.

source.description: The document, message or record the words came from, with its date where known.

decision.description: At a review, only when the owner has said it: released, the next round of money was released. deferred, the decision was put off. withdrew, the request was withdrawn. Never choose it for the owner.

results.description: At a review: what was measured, by the name of the agreed result.

quote.description: The words as written in the source, at least a few words long.

source.description: The document, message or record the words came from, with its date where known.

kind.description: measured when it was counted from records. Otherwise it is an estimate.

stage.description: What the money is for: discovery before anything is built, a limited pilot, or a rollout. Use the stage the record names.

thresholds.description: Up to three results the owner agreed would release more money, written down before the work starts.

baseline_kind.description: measured when today's figure was counted from records. Otherwise it is an estimate.

direction.description: at_most when lower is better, at_least when higher is better.

quote.description: The words as written in the source, at least a few words long.

source.description: The document, message or record the words came from, with its date where known.

measure.description: What is measured, for example Cost per resolved ticket.

industry.description: Answer or correction in canonical or everyday language, for example retail, hospital, bank or public sector, or unknown when nobody has stated it. Never guess it. Overrides anything read from proposal.

pending_approvals.description: Approvals still to come before the initiative may go live, such as a separate controls sign-off or a go-live decision for one country. Each is one sentence in what, the approver in by only where the record names them, and in evidence mode the quote. They never change the verdict. On an Accelerate the first step says what is pending and to go ahead once it is given. Where the controls themselves are disputed or unproven, that is not a pending approval: answer the risk question as the records stand.

by.description: The person who signs it off. Kept only when the quote names them.

quote.description: The words as written in the source, at least a few words long.

source.description: The document, message or record the words came from, with its date where known.

quote.description: The words as written in the source, at least a few words long.

source.description: The document, message or record the words came from, with its date where known.

what.description: What is pending, in one sentence. For example: France activation is pending separate controls sign-off.

proposal.description: The AI initiative in the user's own words. Pass it unchanged on every call. The tool reads industry, business function, AI type and headcount from it and never guesses an unread value.

readiness.description: Accepted for compatibility and ignored. The front door verdict does not use the operating-model label.

revenue_eur.description: Accepted for compatibility and ignored. The front door verdict does not use revenue.

review.description: At a return visit to an initiative that was assessed before. Pass previous_brief, the brief_url the earlier verdict came with, unchanged: the result then says in since_last which answers changed and which change moved the verdict. Without that link, pass previous_verdict and outcome. A review never changes the verdict. In evidence mode an outcome needs its own quote and source, or it is not kept.

quote.description: The words as written in the source, at least a few words long.

source.description: The document, message or record the words came from, with its date where known.

outcome.description: delivering: it went ahead and is delivering what was expected. falling_short: it went ahead and is falling short. fixed_then_went_ahead: it was fixed first, then went ahead. paused_or_stopped: it was paused or stopped. no_decision: no decision has been made.

previous_brief.description: The brief_url returned with the earlier verdict, passed unchanged. The earlier answers and quotes travel inside it. Nothing is stored.

scores.description: OPTIONAL, for callers that already hold 0 to 100 pillar scores from the user. A regular user answers the guided questions and never needs this. A supplied score takes precedence over an answer. Never invent a number: this tool fills in nothing.

change_enablement.description: Optional; when omitted, estimated from readiness (agile 55, traditional 45, siloed 32 — always below the 60 floor, because an unevidenced change capability is unproven). Sponsor in place, owner named, change budget funded (0–100, higher is better). Must be ≥ 60 for an Accelerate verdict.

financial_return.description: Optional; when omitted, estimated from the disclosed AI BVF planning range for the function (40–52, never enough to clear 60 unmodelled, never low enough to force a Stop). Strength of the modelled return (0–100, higher is better). A value ≤ 20 forces a Stop on its own; ≥ 60 is one of the four conditions required for Accelerate.

governance_risk.description: Optional; when omitted, estimated from tier and regulated context (gen1 30 / gen2 42 / gen3 55, +10 in a regulated function, +8 in a regulated industry — agentic AI in regulated finance estimates at 73 and forces a Stop until governance evidence exists). This pillar is INVERTED: higher means MORE risk. ≥ 70 forces a Stop on its own; must be ≤ 40 for Accelerate.

strategic_alignment.description: Optional; estimated at 50 (unproven) when omitted, since alignment to a board KPI cannot be read from context. How clearly this moves a board-level KPI (0–100, higher is better). Must be ≥ 60 — together with financial_return ≥ 60, change_enablement ≥ 60 and governance_risk ≤ 40 — for an Accelerate verdict.

signal_completeness.description: Optional 0 to 1 input-quality factor. The default ranges from 0.5 when all pillars are estimated to 1 when all are supplied. Supplied values still require evidence review. Lower this factor when the supplied pillars rest on weak evidence.

work_architecture.description: Evidence that workflows, roles, decision rights and measures are ready. Pass only what is known. Explicit gaps and omitted checks block Accelerate until all four checks are evidenced. OPTIONAL, for callers that already hold the four checks. Refused in evidence mode: there, answer work_architecture in answers with a to d and quote it in evidence.

decision_rights_defined.description: True only when decision, override and escalation rights have named human owners, false when authority remains unclear.

measures_updated.description: True only when performance measures and incentives reflect the redesigned work, false when the old measures remain.

roles_redesigned.description: True only when affected roles, accountabilities and capability expectations have been rewritten, false when roles remain unchanged.

workflow_redesigned.description: True only when the end-to-end workflow has been redesigned around the AI and retained human judgement, false when the existing workflow remains.

name: assess_ai_initiative

also_open.description: not_enough_to_judge only. Anything still open after the three in decides.

ambiguous_fields.description: Fields whose wording pointed to more than one value, each with the competing values. Ask the user to choose; never choose for them.

answered_by.description: Present when an agent answered from evidence.

conflicts.description: Evidence mode: answers on which two records disagree. Each was counted as not known. Put ask to the owner, with both sets of quotes beside it, and never say which record is right.

against.description: The words in another record that say otherwise.

quote.description: The words as written in the source, at least a few words long.

source.description: The document, message or record the words came from, with its date where known.

answer.description: The answer the first record supports.

ask.description: The question to put to the owner, in these words.

evidence.description: The words that support that answer.

quote.description: The words as written in the source, at least a few words long.

source.description: The document, message or record the words came from, with its date where known.

short.description: A short name for the question.

context_defaults.description: Company facts the records did not state, and the default used in their place. Say each line with the verdict.

decides.description: not_enough_to_judge only. Up to three things still to answer, most decisive first.

answer_in.description: The input field that carries the answer on the next call.

where_to_look.description: Where the answer is usually written down. Look there before answering unknown.

evidence_missing.description: Evidence mode: answers that came with no quote and source. Each was counted as not known. Find the words, or leave the answer as unknown.

evidence_set_aside.description: Evidence mode: quotes set aside because they give a figure about other organisations, such as a supplier's claim about comparable sites or clients of your size. They do not count for this organisation's return or result. Say each line beside its quote.

funding.description: Present when a funding record was passed, or the earlier brief carried one. Say statement with the verdict, then each line in thresholds and each entry in gaps. Every figure is the organisation's own. Never add a figure, and never say whether to fund: say note.

agreement_changed.description: True when results passed today differ from those the earlier brief carried. The earlier ones are used. Tell the owner.

quote.description: The words as written in the source, at least a few words long.

source.description: The document, message or record the words came from, with its date where known.

amount_eur.description: Set only when the record states euros.

quote.description: The words as written in the source, at least a few words long.

source.description: The document, message or record the words came from, with its date where known.

gaps.description: What the person who holds the budget still does not know, most important first.

note.description: Whose figures these are, and whose decision it is. Say it.

review.description: Present once a result is in.

statement.description: The record in plain sentences. Say it as written.

quote.description: The words as written in the source, at least a few words long.

source.description: The document, message or record the words came from, with its date where known.

line.description: The agreed result in one sentence. Say it as written.

met.description: At a review: whether the result is on the agreed side of the target.

quote.description: The words as written in the source, at least a few words long.

source.description: The document, message or record the words came from, with its date where known.

inferred_fields.description: Fields read from the wording of the proposal instead of an explicit answer.

next_question.description: The one thing to ask the user next, as a sentence. Absent when status is verdict.

open_questions.description: Evidence mode only. Every guided question still without an answer, each with its choices and where to look. Answer all of them in one call, each with its quote, and unknown where you found nothing. On a verdict nothing waits on them: answer them and call again, and the brief carries those answers too.

answer_in.description: The input field that carries the answer on the next call.

where_to_look.description: Where the answer is usually written down. Look there before answering unknown.

pending_approvals.description: Approvals still to come before go-live. Say each line with the verdict. On an Accelerate the first step already carries them: never tell the owner to go ahead without them.

quote.description: The words as written in the source, at least a few words long.

source.description: The document, message or record the words came from, with its date where known.

proposal.description: The supplied proposal, returned so the next call can preserve it verbatim.

question.description: The same question in structured form. Show the question and every choice label to the user, in the given order, and pass back the id of the choice they pick in the field named by answer_in. Ask one question per turn.

number.description: Guided questions only: position in the sequence.

where_to_look.description: Guided questions only: where the answer is usually written down.

why.description: Why the answer decides the outcome.

resolutions.description: Every deterministic resolution, naming the field, canonical value, source and matched phrase.

resolved_inputs.description: Context resolved so far: industry, function, ai_tier, employees and track (smaller_firm under 250 people, otherwise enterprise).

review.description: Present when a review was passed: the earlier verdict and what happened since. accepted is false when an agent gave an outcome with no evidence.

quote.description: The words as written in the source, at least a few words long.

source.description: The document, message or record the words came from, with its date where known.

since_last.description: Present when previous_brief was passed. Say statement with the verdict, then each line in changes with the earlier and the new quote beside it.

changes.description: Each answer that differs from the earlier verdict.

from.description: The answer as it stood then, with its quotes.

moved_verdict.description: True when putting this one answer back gives a different outcome from today's.

to.description: The answer today, with its quotes.

context_changed.description: Present when the earlier brief was for another industry, function, AI type or size. Tell the owner.

previous_date.description: The date of the earlier verdict, written YYYY-MM-DD.

statement.description: What changed, in plain sentences. Say it as written.

unchanged.description: How many of the five answers are the same as before.

status.description: needs_input: a piece of context is unread, ask question. needs_confirmation: show understood and ask the user to confirm or correct it. not_enough_to_judge: ask question, the next guided question. verdict: Accelerate, Fix or Stop from the user's answers only.

suggestions.description: Accepted values for an explicitly supplied field that could not be resolved.

to_find_out.description: Questions the user answered with "I do not know yet". A verdict waits on these. When no question is left to ask, tell the user to find these out and come back.

answer_in.description: The input field that carries the answer on the next call.

where_to_look.description: Where the answer is usually written down. Look there before answering unknown.

understood.description: Plain statement of how the proposal was read. Show it to the user before anything else and invite corrections.

verdict.description: Present only when status is verdict. Rests on what the user answered or supplied, read against the words of the proposal. Carries no euro figure and no estimated score.

answers_given.description: The guided answers behind those scores: the choice, its wording and the published score it carries.

audit.description: Reproducibility record: engine version, the rules that fired, and the resolved inputs. Deterministic, no timestamps. If the verdict is challenged months later, the same inputs on the same engine version reproduce it exactly.

inputs_used.description: The resolved inputs the result was computed on, including estimated pillar values.

rules_fired.description: The rules that actually fired, in order: estimation, gates, classification, value arithmetic.

brief_url.description: A link to the one-page brief for this verdict, to forward to the person who has to sign it off. The context, the answers and any quoted evidence travel inside the link after the # sign and are stored nowhere. Show it behind link text where the chat can do that. Never change it and never pass it to a link shortener. Absent when the verdict rests on a supplied score.

contradictions.description: Where the words of the proposal contradict a favourable answer. Empty when they agree. Any entry holds the verdict at Fix until the user changes the proposal or the answer. Quote proposal_words beside answer and ask which one is true.

found_in.description: Where the words were found. Absent means the proposal.

proposal_says.description: What those words say about the initiative.

proposal_words.description: The words as written in the proposal.

rule.description: The published phrase rule that fired.

decision_confidence.description: Heuristic decision score, 0 to 100, with no probability calibration. Present only when all four pillars were supplied.

feedback.description: Optional three-question feedback route, present only for Fix/Stop verdicts. The page records the response anonymously only when the user chooses an answer; no assessment data is attached.

first_step.description: The one thing to do first. Give it after the summary.

holding_back.description: The answers that keep the initiative from a go-ahead, most decisive first. Empty for Accelerate. Show each with what the user said and what it needs to become.

evidence.description: Evidence mode: the words this answer rests on and where they were found, one entry per quote. Show them beside the answer.

quote.description: The words as written in the source, at least a few words long.

source.description: The document, message or record the words came from, with its date where known.

needed.description: What the answer has to become to clear the bar.

proposal_words.description: Present when the proposal or the evidence contradicts this answer: the words as written. Quote them to the user.

short.description: A short name for the question, for lists.

interpretation.description: How to read decision_confidence. Present only when all four pillars were supplied.

method_note.description: Present only for Fix/Stop verdicts: where the method and the code are published. It carries no offer.

provenance.description: Evidence mode only. Say statement with the verdict, so nobody takes an agent's reading for a person's answer.

reason.description: The rule that produced the classification, in framework terms. For audit use; prefer summary when speaking to the user.

scores_supplied.description: The pillar scores the verdict rests on, from answers or supplied scores. Nothing here was estimated.

summary.description: The outcome in one or two plain sentences. A Stop quotes its cause. Lead with this.

value_note.description: Why no euro figure is given.

verdict_flips.description: The nearest single-pillar movements that change the verdict. Present only when all four pillars were supplied.

work_architecture.description: The work architecture gate across workflow, roles, human decision rights and performance measures. A stated gap or missing evidence blocks Accelerate.

warning.description: A condition the user must meet first. Lead with it when present.
